clue.text: An Australian about fifty becomes a snob

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, here the Australian round the number

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate, so an Australian is one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An Australian turns snooty on reaching fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snob' looks like a social climber, but it is an old word for a shoemaker. The 'X' in the held text is an OCR artefact from the hyphen in 'be-comes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snob is an old dialect name for a shoemaker or mender of boots, the trade of the answer.

clue.text: They may rise to high figures…

definitions.text: They may rise to high figures…

parts.words: They may rise to high figures
parts.note: pillars rise to statues on top, and lists of numbers add up to big totals

explanation.surface: Things that climb to great heights or numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's statue tops the pillar in Trafalgar Square; a ledger's vertical lists of numbers also climb to high totals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillars carry statues aloft, and vertical lists of numbers in accounts can reach large totals.

clue.text: No bias can change them, or their convictions

definitions.text: No bias can change them, or their convictions

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters in no bias can

explanation.surface: Believers whose opinions no argument can shift.
explanation.walkthrough: These are people who hold that Francis Bacon wrote Shakespeare's plays, a conviction notoriously immune to argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the theory that Francis Bacon wrote Shakespeare are famously unshakeable in that belief.

clue.text: Thread your way in Cumberland by car

indicators.note: by means placed beside the car, so the car is what goes with this piece to make the city and is taken away

parts.note: Carlisle is the chief city of the old county of Cumberland
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thread your way through Cumberland in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is the county town of Cumberland in north-west England; the answer set by CAR makes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine, hard-twisted cotton yarn used for stockings is a type of thread.

clue.text: "When——was an actor in Rome" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a quotation with a gap: Hamlet's line names a famous actor of ancient Rome, whose name fills the blank

explanation.surface: Fill the gap in a line from Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet, Act 2 scene 2: 'When Roscius was an actor in Rome', mocking Polonius's stale news.
explanation.definitionFit: The most celebrated comic actor of the Roman Republic is the name Shakespeare puts in that line.

clue.text: Clerical wear found in accountant's wardrobe ?

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, plus the possessive 's
a sock is an item found in anyone's wardrobe of clothes

explanation.surface: A priest's robe turns up among an accountant's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as CA'S SOCK: the accountant's sock, which would indeed be found in his wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, close-fitting robe worn by clergy and choristers is a standard piece of clerical dress.

clue.text: Clothes that make a difference

definitions.meaning: fresh sets of garments to put on

explanation.definitionFit: Spare sets of garments are this, and the verb meaning alters is the same word.

clue.text: A singularly quiet game?

parts.note: singularly means alone, by oneself
whist is an old adjective meaning silent or hushed

explanation.surface: A game played alone in silence?
explanation.walkthrough: This is a card game in which one player may bid to play alone against the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game derived from whist, in which a player can contract to take tricks alone.

clue.text: One instrumental in doing voluntary work

definitions.text: One instrumental in doing voluntary work

parts.words: One instrumental in doing voluntary work
parts.note: a voluntary is a piece played in church before or after a service, so the instrument does it

explanation.surface: A key figure in charity work.
explanation.definitionFit: A church voluntary is a solo piece played on the pipe instrument, which is literally instrumental in it.

clue.text: Where to get some potty ideas on, house-craft ?

definitions.text: Where to get some potty ideas on, house-craft

parts.words: Where to get some potty ideas on, house-craft
parts.note: potty seems to mean daft, but the room where pots are used gives ideas on housekeeping

explanation.surface: Where to pick up some crazy household tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The room for cooking, full of pots and pans, is where one learns the craft of running a house.

clue.text: Hair fasteners

definitions.meaning: devices that secure doors and gates with a key

explanation.definitionFit: Tresses of hair, and also mechanisms that secure doors, share this one word.

clue.text: It can be spotted in a twinkling

definitions.text: It can be spotted in a twinkling

parts.words: It can be spotted in a twinkling
parts.note: seen as a twinkle, it is literally visible in twinkling points in the night sky; the surface suggests something seen in an instant

explanation.surface: Something noticed in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from distant suns appears to twinkle, so it is seen in a twinkling rather than in an instant.

clue.text: A novel guy

parts.note: Guy is the first name of the title hero of a Walter Scott novel, so the clue names a novel by its Guy

explanation.surface: An unusual chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's novel Guy Mannering takes its title from its hero, literally a novel Guy.

clue.text: This crank might give you a lift

definitions.text: This crank might give you a lift

parts.words: This crank might give you a lift
parts.note: a crank here is a handle turned to hoist loads, not an eccentric offering a ride

explanation.surface: An eccentric driver might offer you a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoisting device worked by a cranked handle raises loads, giving them a lift.

clue.text: Some have a rolling gait

parts.note: a rolling gait suggests sailors, but those on roller skates move on rolling wheels

explanation.surface: Some people walk with a sailor's swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: Those on roller skates glide along on rolling wheels, a literally rolling gait.

clue.text: Type-setters as it were

parts.note: printers set type, but models that set the standard for a type are its patterns

explanation.surface: Printers, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Models or patterns are perfect specimens that establish a type for others to copy.

clue.text: Patron saint of umbrella-makers?

parts.note: the saint whose feast day is said to bring forty days of rain would be good for the umbrella trade

explanation.surface: Which saint looks after umbrella manufacturers?
explanation.walkthrough: English folklore says that if it rains on this saint's day, 15 July, it will rain for forty days.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore ties this Winchester bishop's feast day to forty days of rain, which would make him the umbrella trade's friend.

clue.text: Trouble with the cockles ?

parts.note: cockles look like shellfish, but the cockles of the heart are its innermost feelings

explanation.surface: A problem with shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow or grief afflicts the cockles of one's heart, the seat of deep feeling.

clue.text: The loss they make is not apparent

definitions.text: The loss they make is not apparent

indicators.note: the words the loss are present but disguised, their letters rearranged so they cannot be seen

explanation.surface: Hostels run at a hidden loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters rearranged spell THE LOSS, so the loss they make is there but not apparent.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget lodging houses for travellers are the 'they' of the clue, whose own letters hide the loss.

clue.text: He had to become a wild man

indicators.note: become says these letters turn into something else, a new word

explanation.surface: Circumstances forced him to turn savage.
explanation.definitionFit: An impetuous, rash person who flares up easily is a wild, uncontrolled sort.

clue.text: A literary underminer, one of them

definitions.text: A literary underminer, one of them

parts.words: A literary underminer, one of them
parts.note: Sapper was the pen name of the author of the Bulldog Drummond stories, and military engineers dig tunnels under enemy works

explanation.surface: A critic who undermines writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Military engineers who dig saps under fortifications are underminers, and Sapper was a novelist's pen name.

clue.text: Not to be taken out of London

definitions.text: Not to be taken out of London

parts.words: Not to be taken out of London
parts.note: a railway service heading towards the capital will carry you in, never out

explanation.surface: Something that must not be removed from London.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways 'up' means towards London, so an up train runs into the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: In British railway usage a service travelling towards London is the up service, so it never takes you out.

clue.text: Use lint to make something useful

indicators.note: to make signals that the letters of use lint are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Turn lint to some useful purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or implement, especially in the kitchen, is a useful object.

clue.text: Just the rhymes for gardeners ?

parts.note: the word that comes before rhymes for children also names a place where young plants are raised

explanation.surface: Ideal verses for gardeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's rhymes carry this name, and so does a garden centre raising young plants.

clue.text: One may be encountered in land or sea lanes

definitions.text: One may be encountered in land or sea lanes

parts.words: One may be encountered in land or sea lanes
parts.note: a vagrant walks country lanes and a cargo steamer without fixed route plies shipping lanes, both called by one word

explanation.surface: Someone you might meet on country lanes or shipping routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant wanders country roads, and a cargo ship with no fixed route is a steamer of the same name.

clue.text: It's right in the corner of the Square

definitions.text: It's right in the corner of the Square

parts.words: It's right in the corner of the Square
parts.note: every corner of a square holds a ninety-degree corner, a right one

explanation.surface: It is just there in the corner of the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: Each corner of a square forms a right one, ninety degrees.

clue.text: Poor bard sampling The Raven?

parts.note: The Raven is the famous poem by Edgar Allan Poe, standing for its author
one sampling food or wine is a taster

explanation.surface: A bad poet tries out Poe's famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as POE TASTER: someone sampling Poe. The suffix -aster marks something inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of inferior verse is a poor bard, a would-be poet.

clue.text: Give everything back to share out

parts.note: everything means all

indicators.note: back tells you the little word to is turned round

explanation.surface: Return everything so it can be divided up.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion or distribute portions is to divide and share them out.

clue.text: Their work is stylish and incisive

definitions.text: Their work is stylish and incisive

parts.words: Their work is stylish and incisive
parts.note: stylish suggests elegant but means done with a stylus, and incisive means cut into metal

explanation.surface: Praise for elegant, sharp-minded workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who cut designs into metal with a graver or stylus do work that is literally incised.

clue.text: Alice uncommonly well-fed on treacle

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the name Alice is rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice is remarkably plump from eating treacle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters, Elsie, Lacie and Tillie, who lived at the bottom of a treacle well; 'well-fed' puns on that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dormouse's tale has this sister living in a treacle well and eating treacle, so she is fed from a well of it.

clue.text: Arrays in line

parts.note: arrays as a verb means clothes, while to set soldiers in straight ranks is the drill sense of the same verb

explanation.surface: Sets things out in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both clothes someone finely and, in drill, aligns troops in a straight rank.

clue.text: It might provide a chance to break the law

definitions.text: It might provide a chance to break the law

parts.words: It might provide a chance to break the law
parts.note: a draw of tickets offers a chance of a prize, and private ones were long illegal

explanation.surface: An opportunity for crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize draw is a game of chance, and running one privately was long against the law.
